html:
SMTO-LLM-0012 — Model stream exceeded a transport safety limit

GUID: 7aa902b5-1946-417b-88ea-389bac682e34
Slug: llm-stream-total-size-limit
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • The model's reply grew past the most SMTO will collect for one reply (about 32 MB, including thinking you don't see). SMTO stopped it, and nothing from it was carried out.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Below the message box, turn Thinking off or lower the Output limit for this conversation (select Controls if you don't see them). Hidden thinking and long output both count toward this size, so a shorter reply stays under the limit.
  2. Ask for the work in smaller parts, for example one file or one section at a time. Each smaller request produces a smaller reply.
  3. Then ask SMTO to continue in a new message, saying which steps are already done. These composer changes apply to new messages, and SMTO did not act on the oversized reply, so nothing from it needs undoing.

What success looks like

  • The model's reply finishes and the task moves on without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the model server; the model may be producing far more output than it should. Don't turn off SMTO's safety checks to get past this limit.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The provider's SSE stream exceeded the decoder's fixed 32 MiB total limit, which counts framing, ignored fields and hidden reasoning (llm_stream_total_size_limit).

What this means

  • The decoder counted more than 32 MiB across the stream, including ignored fields and hidden reasoning. This is a transport safety bound, not proof that the model’s input context was full.

Why this can happen

  • Total received stream bytes exceeded MAX_STREAM_BYTES.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare total response bytes and repeated or hidden fields in a sanitized provider test. Check output settings only if excessive generated output explains the byte count.

How to fix it

  • Inspect chunks_received, actionable_output_characters, reasoning_or_unknown_stream_events and llm_max_tokens in provider_diagnostic. Reduce the role's Output allowance or thinking budget, or split the task, so the whole stream stays under MAX_STREAM_BYTES (32 MiB, fixed in src/agent_runtime/llm/sse.py); if visible output is small but the stream is huge, check the provider for oversized per-event metadata or runaway reasoning.
  • Ask the provider operator to check the stream format and byte limits with a small test request. Preserve prior tool receipts; do not replay completed operations.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The full controlled response completes below the 32 MiB stream bound.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • The bounded stream decoder rejects the current response; it does not rewrite earlier tool receipts.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
